recognize_zh: 單一漿細胞：偏心圓形細胞核、核旁淡染區（hof），細胞質深紫色且周邊帶有偏紅紫的色調，這種細胞質邊緣呈火焰般紅紫色的漿細胞稱為火焰細胞（flame cell）。
features: Single large plasma cell with abundant cytoplasm and eccentric round nucleus
Coarse, clock-face-like clumped chromatin without visible nucleolus
Pale perinuclear hof (Golgi zone) adjacent to the nucleus
Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a reddish-purple (fuchsinophilic) tinge toward the periphery
Surrounding red cells are unremarkable; background shows fine precipitate
describe_en: Smear shows a single large plasma cell with an eccentric round nucleus containing coarsely clumped chromatin, a perinuclear hof, and abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a reddish-purple peripheral tinge. This fuchsinophilic cytoplasmic coloration, attributed to glycoprotein-rich (often IgA) immunoglobulin, defines a flame cell. Flame cells can be seen in plasma cell myeloma, particularly IgA type, but are not by themselves diagnostic of a clonal process. Findings are consistent with a flame cell; clonality should be assessed by light-chain restriction and plasma cell quantitation.

ddx.vs: Mott cells contain multiple pale round Russell bodies (grape-like vacuoles) rather than diffuse reddish-purple peripheral cytoplasm.
Plasmacytoid lymphocytes are smaller with less abundant cytoplasm and lack the prominent hof and fuchsinophilic rim.
Basophilic normoblasts have a central round nucleus with a thin rim of deep blue cytoplasm and no perinuclear hof or eccentric placement.
Thesaurocytes contain fibrillary crystalline cytoplasmic inclusions and a larger cell outline rather than a uniform flame-colored periphery.
